row.notes: TyreComponent::changeToNextCompound. Log channel PITSTOP_TYRES: 'TyreComponent::changeToNextCompound %p - PITLANE CHANGEOVER' (0x142e940b4) | 'MOX/Tyres: changeToNextCompound() new type %d is not the same as next type '%s' (from %d)' (0x142e9420d). rcx = the TyreComponent (kept in rsi), dl = pit_stop (kept in ebx, tested at 0x142e941eb and 0x142e94219). Two callers, neither reads the result: Game_PitLane_ApplyPitstopTyres passes 1 (mov dl,1 at 0x1434bdd9d, call at 0x1434bdd9f) and then calls pitstopComplete 0x142e94780 (0x1434bde3f) behind the same m_tyreList[idx] bound and null test (0x1434bdd8b/0x1434bdd9b and 0x1434bde31/0x1434bde3d), so it runs exactly when this call did and both are skipped, with a log line each, for a null entry; Game_PitBoxCarActor_Update passes 0 (xor edx,edx at 0x1403c8dd1, call at 0x1403c8dd3). The body finds the next set by the id at +0x9c70 among the 0x18-byte entries from +0x9bd0 (count +0x9c48), falling back to id 4 when that id is 3 or more (unsigned) and to id 1 otherwise (0x142e9412e..0x142e9415c). When it differs from the fitted set (+0x9938 id, +0x9940, +0x9948) it logs the second line (the fitted id from +0x9938, the found entry's name, the found id) and then, with pit_stop set, calls 0x142e96390 (0x142e941f2) instead of storing the set at +0x9938..+0x9948 itself (0x142e9421d..0x142e94231). It then calls 0x142ea1d30 and, unless +0x9c70 is -1, 0x142e9eda0(component+0x9c60, component+0x9c70, that result) (0x142e9425a), ORs dword +0x208 & 0x1f of every tyre record (records at +0x30, stride 0xde0, count u64 +0x98d0; 0x142e94280..0x142e9428a) into ebp, calls 0x142e83130(record, k, 0, 0) for k = 0..4 on every record (0x142e942cb..0x142e943ce), and picks a record by the id in dword [[+0x9c98]-0x6c] (same fallback) whose entry holds at +0x10 a qword pointer (loaded at 0x142e944ad) to the byte (read at 0x142e944b8) that indexes the byte table [[+0x9bc0]+0x1d8], giving the record +0x30 + that byte * 0xde0 (0x142e94412..0x142e944cd); unless [+0x20] is 0 (0x142e944a7) for k = 0..3 it calls 0x142e83130(that record, k, bit k of the OR when byte +0x9915 is set, 0) and 0x142e87870 with the same value, then 0x142e87870 again for k = 0..3 with the bare bit, and for bit 4 0x142e83130(that record, 4, bit 4, 0) and, when +0x98f8 is set, 0x142e87ab0 (0x142e944d0..0x142e946a8); calls 0x142ea2300(component, 1, 0x101) and returns 0 (xor eax,eax at 0x142e946bc, its one exit). pitstopComplete (a jmp to 0x14f43e230) clears +0x9910 and calls 0x142e83130/0x142e87540 only on the +0x4a0 and +0x940 sub-records of each tyre record, for k = 0..5 (0x142e83130 returns at once for k above 4, 0x142e83262) (log 'MOX/Tyres: pitstopComplete() disabling everything but set %d'). Steam 1.0.145: the same code at 0x142e965d0 (sigport --witness 406/406, with +0x30, +0x98d0, +0x238, +0xde0, +0x9938, +0x9940, +0x9948 and +0x9915 at the same instructions). 0x142e83130 is setTyreVisibility (log 'setTyreVisibility %p m_tyreModelVisibility %x', 0x142e8337c): it sets bit k of dword +0x208 when its third argument is true (lock or at 0x142e83294) and clears it otherwise (0x142e8329f), so +0x208 & 0x1f is the record's tyre model visibility mask, not damage, and the OR is the set of parts shown on any record. | re-bindings 2026-11-18: raised to L2 for the core's race tyre change rule (native/src/core/guards/garage/pit_box.cpp).
